sentences.text: The case of the prosecution is that a complaint was lodged by CW.1 stating that a person named Sri. K.N.Rajashekar had visited him on 16.07.1998 claiming that a cheque drawn by southern Railways for a sum of Rs.9,987/- towards refund of EMD in his favour was wrongly encashed in an account at the post office, Rajajinagar.
On verification, he found that the said EMD was encashed in an account held by Smt. B.K. Manoranjithamma.

On further enquiry, it was noticed that the person who had opened the account of Smt. B.K. Manoranjithamma had also opened three other accounts in the names of Sri. D.V. Manjunath, Sri. Madhava Ravindra and Smt. Vidya Ravindra.
CW.1 instructed the savings bank counter personnel not to entertain any cheques in the above accounts and inform him, in case any of the above account holders turn up at the post office.
He stated that a person got two dividend warrants of Rs.385/- in the name of Sri Madhava Ravindra on 20.07.1998.
The savings bank counter personnel alerted CW.1 about the person, who vanished before CW.1 could reach the counter.
On 31.07.1998 two persons went to the counter to collect pass book and to deposit seven dividend warrants in the account of Smt.Vidya Ravindra, valued at Rs.5,443/-.
CW.1 managed to take one of them to his chamber and when questioned, he disclosed his name as C.Raju but did not give any particulars.
On the same day a person named Sri Madhu Bhaskar visited the post office at 5.00 p.m. and informed CW.1 that Sri C.Raju was his relative and sought help.

On enquiry, he revealed that he was working in the office of Chief Engineer, Southern Railways in receipts section and claimed that Sri M.K.Nagendra Kumar opened all the accounts and the dividend warrants and cheques were brought by him to the post office for crediting into the respective accounts and also that he withdrew the amount.

Sri. Madhu Bhaskar disclosed that he had removed the warrants and cheques received by post and handed them over to Sri. M.K.
Nagendra Kumar and that all the vouchers, deposit slips, withdrawal slips and cheques were in the handwriting of Sri. M.K.Nagendra Kumar.

He claimed that Sri. M.K.Nagendra Kumar got a rubber stamp in the name of M/s.Rajashekar Associates to enable him to obtain the cheque for Rs.9,987/-
dated 16.01.1998 favouring Rajshekar Associates and credited into the savings bank account of Smt.
B.K.Manjoranjithamma.

CW.1 alleged that the total amount fraudulently withdrawn by Sri.
M.K.Nagendra Kumar was Rs.12,804.50Ps.
CW.1 therefore requested the police to take suitable action against the accused and enclosed the relevant documents.
The jurisdictional Police, secured the presence of accused No.1 and seized two pass books of Smt. B.K. Manoranjithamma and Sri.

The Trial Court therefore convicted the accused No.1 for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420 and 465 of IPC and sentenced him to undergo simple imprisonment for six months and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 419 of IPC and to undergo simple imprisonment for one year and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 420 of IPC and to undergo simple imprisonment for seven months and to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 465 of IPC.

It was ordered that all the sentences of simple imprisonment shall run one after another and that the accused No.1 was entitled to set off the period of imprisonment already undergone as under trial prisoner against the sentence of imprisonment.

In so far as accused No.3 is concerned, there was no evidence to establish the guilt against him and therefore, the Trial Court acquitted him of the offences punishable under Sections 419, 465 and 420 of IPC.

The evidence of PW.1 - 19 - sand PW.2 established the role of accused No.1 and the report of the forensic expert (PW.6) sealed the fate of accused No.1 in as much as his admitted signatures corresponded with the signatures found on the account opening forms to open the accounts in the names of Sri. Madhava Ravindra and Smt. Vidya Ravindra as well as the pay-in and withdrawal slips into and from the account of Sri.
Madhava Ravindra and Smt. Vidya Ravindra, while they did not match with the admitted signature of Sri. Madhava Ravindra and Smt. Vidya Ravindra.
The seizure of the pass books (Exs.P27 and 28)
and the cheque book (Ex.P29) was not disputed by accused No.1.
The totality of evidence more particularly the evidence of PW.4 and PW.2 and the evidence of PW.6 proved the case of the prosecution beyond doubt.
The Trial Court was therefore justified in returning a finding of guilt of the accused No.1 for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420 and 465 of IPC and in passing the impugned Judgment of conviction and order of sentence.
The Appellate Court too re-appreciated the evidence on record and rightly upheld the Judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed by the Trial Court.
